message.content: Run an eight-week pilot in two comparable sections, such as mysteries and contemporary fiction, using a small “Try Someone New” face-out display at the end of each aisle rather than rearranging the main shelves. Each display should hold 12 titles by lesser-known authors, selected to resemble popular nearby writers in tone, genre, and price, with a simple shelf card reading, for example, “If you enjoy Tana French, try Jane Harper.” Keep all books in their normal alphabetical locations as well, so customers can still browse predictably. Alternate the featured authors every two weeks and use different recommendation pairings in the two sections. Track unit sales of featured titles, total sales in each genre, and whether customers buy a featured author alongside a familiar author. Ask a short optional checkout question: “Did you find what you came for easily?” and “Did you discover an author new to you?” Compare results with the same eight-week period last year or with similar unfeatured sections. Staff should note common customer reactions and any confusion caused by the displays. If discovery sales rise without lowering reported ease of navigation or disrupting genre sales, expand the displays gradually to other sections; if not, refine the recommendations, signage, or placement before scaling.
